id: d-001
genre: decisions
title: "Ledgerline stores its data in SQLite"
created: 2026-02-18
provenance: hand-authored
tags: [ledgerline, storage]
status: accepted
related:
  - type: influenced_by
    to: references/sqlite-wal-notes.md

---

Context: Ledgerline needs a datastore for timesheets, invoices, and client
records. Studio write volume is small — one billing run a month plus daily
timesheets.

Options considered: Postgres (operational weight, a server to babysit)
versus SQLite (single file, WAL mode, embedded).

Decision: use SQLite in WAL mode as the sole datastore for Ledgerline v1;
Postgres stays out of scope until a second-writer need appears.

Consequences: zero server operations; backups are file copies; the
single-writer ceiling is accepted. Informed by the WAL-mode reading notes
(sqlite-wal-notes).

---

Wayfare is Meridian Studio's realtime departure-display program for Halcyon
Transit: platform displays for three pilot stations — Ashport Central, Ferry
Quay, Millbrook Bridge — fed by live vehicle-position data.

Scope agreed at the kickoff (2026-02-20) with Petra Lindqvist: sub-second
perceived freshness, outdoor readability, and a June ship date. The displays
speak MQTT (decision d-002) and went from per-display autonomy (d-003) to an
edge-gateway hub (d-008) after field maintenance pain. The palette is
green-and-amber for outdoor readability (d-009).

Team: Dev Okonkwo (firmware), Noor Haddad (renderer), June Park (design),
Bram Oyelaran (fleet), Katrin Ilic (QA), Theo Kanda (systems).
Shipped 2026-06-12; ship retro in m-008.

---
id: d-008
genre: decisions
title: "Wayfare moves to an edge-gateway hub per station"
created: 2026-04-08
provenance: hand-authored
tags: [wayfare, architecture]
status: accepted
related:
  - type: supersedes
    to: decisions/d-003.md
  - type: influenced_by
    to: sessions/s-004.md
  - type: influenced_by
    to: meetings/m-005.md
  - type: mentions
    to: projects/wayfare.md
---

Context: after six weeks in the field, per-display autonomy shows its cost —
firmware drift across boards and roughly ninety minutes of manual reflash per
display when updates land (documented in s-004, reviewed in m-005).

Options considered: keep per-display autonomy with a better flashing ritual;
one edge gateway per station coordinating its displays.

Decision: each pilot station gets an edge gateway hub — firmware flashes once
per station, displays pull from the gateway, telemetry funnels through it.
This supersedes d-003.

Consequences: one more box per station, collapsed maintenance surface; Bram
owns gateway provisioning.

Theo and Dev spent the day in the field at Ashport Central and Ferry Quay:

firmware versions, and a board that lost power would not recover its clock.
Reflashing takes roughly ninety minutes per display carried to the platform.
Per-display autonomy (d-003) is failing on maintenance, not on rendering.

id: fleet-provisioning-notes
genre: references
title: "Provisioning device fleets — ops note"
created: 2026-04-06
provenance: hand-authored
tags: [infrastructure, ops-note]
source: "internal ops note"
related:
  - type: relates_to
    to: references/embedded-single-board-notes.md
---

Provisioning a fleet of small boards two ways: point-wise flashing scales
linearly with board count and fails quietly; a gateway-hub topology flashes
once per site and funnels telemetry home. The hub costs one more box per
station but collapses the maintenance surface.

Written after the Wayfare field pain (s-004); the hub topology is the
direction d-008 adopted.

final_answer:
The fleet-provisioning ops note explicitly links the Wayfare field pain to the edge-gateway decision:

1. **The ops note** (fleet-provisioning-notes.md) states it was "Written after the Wayfare field pain (s-004); the hub topology is the direction d-008 adopted." [references/fleet-provisioning-notes.md, lines 9-12]

2. **The Wayfare field pain (s-004)** documents that after six weeks in the field, per-display autonomy caused "firmware drift across boards and roughly ninety minutes of manual reflash per display when updates land" — boards lost clock on power loss, and three stations drifted to three firmware versions. [sessions/s-004.md, lines 7-10]

3. **The edge-gateway decision (d-008)** cites this exact pain as its context: "after six weeks in the field, per-display autonomy shows its cost — firmware drift across boards and roughly ninety minutes of manual reflash per display when updates land (documented in s-004, reviewed in m-005)." It then decides on "one edge gateway per station coordinating its displays" so "firmware flashes once per station, displays pull from the gateway." [decisions/d-008.md, lines 7-15]

The ops note directly bridges them: the field pain (s-004) motivated the hub topology that decision d-008 adopted.
